verdict.rationale: Companies House has a real, documented REST API with registered keys and a structured auth model. It covers the read side of the register: live company data retrieved by simple GET requests on per-record URIs. The UI does much more than read, though: filing accounts, changing a registered office address, ordering certificates, following companies and checking name availability. Nothing in the evidence shows the API exposes these write or transactional actions, and identity verification is being rolled across the write paths. Missing for 10: API coverage of filing and update actions (accounts, registered office changes), certificate ordering and follow-company features, and evidence of documented parity between the API and the web service.
